componentAcceptance: All T12 criteria are covered. A single real Task plan concurrently runs the actual CLI Task backend with an offline native child/grandchild fixture and a real Linux Docker remote-command backend. Whole-plan cancellation leaves both packages cancelled with one original attempt each, the dependent join skipped and no second CLI process. The CLI receipt has native-tree stop proof; /proc confirms both owned PIDs ended. The remote receipt has container-supervisor stop proof and only one original Agent operation. Existing plan tests retain cancelling and prohibit retry when stop is unconfirmed.
productAcceptance: T12 passes at integration level. Mixed CLI/remote-command trees stop their owned process trees and skip unstarted packages; unknown stop remains nonterminal. implementation: No product code changed. The new acceptance probe composes the real Task service, CLI execution backend, native supervisor, remote machine directory, Agent and Docker command backend.

The probe checks Task attempt counts, exact stop provenance, Linux /proc process termination and original remote operation cardinality.
